value.body: Assistant engineers in a state public works department (PWD) plan, estimate and supervise government roads, bridges and buildings, and manage contractors and works budgets. Most posts are in the civil wing; electrical and mechanical wings recruit separately. It is a field-oriented engineering job in government.

items.label: Typical eligibility
items.note: Mostly civil; junior engineer posts usually take diploma holders

items.label: Who recruits
items.note: Often through a state engineering services exam

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A degree in civil (or electrical/mechanical for those wings) engineering. Apply to the state PSC's assistant engineer recruitment — usually a written exam (sometimes prelims and mains) and in some states an interview. Domicile and state-language requirements are common.

value.title: At a glance
items: Recruitment calendars are irregular and vary by state.
Work is site-based: inspections, measurements, billing and contractor supervision.
Promotions run through executive, superintending and chief engineer levels over a long career.
